title: How Python runs your code
summary: Top to bottom, one line at a time. Comments are skipped, and an error stops everything after it.

intro.text:
When you run a program, Python starts at the first line and works down, **one line at a time**. A line can only use names that earlier lines already made.

A line that starts with `#` is a **comment**: a note for people. Python skips it. You can also put a comment at the end of a line.

If a line goes wrong while it runs, Python **stops right there** and shows an error. The lines after it never run. Some mistakes, like a missing quote, are found before anything runs at all, so nothing prints.

On your own Mac you can do the same thing in Terminal: save the code in a file and run `python3 my_file.py`, or type `python3` to get the `>>>` prompt, which runs one line at a time.
intro.analogy: A program is like a recipe card. You follow the steps from top to bottom. Notes in the margin are for you, not steps. If a step says "add the sauce" and there is no sauce, you stop cooking right there and the later steps never happen.

predict.why: Line 2 starts with #, so it is a comment and Python skips it. The other two lines run in order, top to bottom.

quiz.q: In which order does Python run the lines of a program?
options: Top to bottom, one at a time
quiz.why: Python starts at line 1 and works down, finishing each line before the next.

quiz.q: What does Python do with the line `# total = 5`?
quiz.why: Everything after # is a comment, so the whole line is skipped.

quiz.q: A program has 5 lines. Line 3 causes a NameError. Which lines run?
options: Lines 1 and 2, then it stops at line 3
quiz.why: Python runs lines 1 and 2, stops at the error on line 3, and never reaches lines 4 and 5.

quiz.q: Which mistake stops the program before any line runs at all?
options: Using a name before it is made
A typo in a variable name
quiz.why: Python reads the whole file before it starts. A missing quote means it cannot even read it, so nothing runs. The other mistakes are only found when that line runs.

quiz.q: At the >>> prompt you make `city = "Lima"`, then type just `city` and press Enter. What happens?
quiz.why: The >>> prompt shows the value of whatever you type. In a saved file you need print to see it.

quiz.q: What is the comment in `speed = 30  # in km per hour`?
quiz.why: A comment starts at # and runs to the end of the line. The code before it still runs.

mistakes.title: A space at the start of a line
mistakes.explain: Spaces at the start of a line mean something in Python (you will use them in Unit 2). A stray space where none belongs is an IndentationError, and nothing runs.

mistakes.title: A missing closing quote
mistakes.explain: The text starts with a quote but never ends, so Python cannot read the line. It stops before running anything, even the lines before it.

gen.error: SyntaxError: unterminated string literal (detected at line 1)

mistakes.title: A typo in print
mistakes.explain: Python only knows print, not pritn. To Python it is a name that does not exist. The error message even suggests what you meant.

gen.error: NameError: name 'pritn' is not defined. Did you mean: 'print'?
